notes:
Summary: Aurum runs an enterprise media archive (broadcast transcripts, long-form articles, digitized magazines). Primary need: RAG-powered search over very long documents with strong relevance and predictable latency at scale. They want embeddings + a lightweight reranker for precision.

Key constraints (quoted):
- "We need sub-second search for editors across 10M+ items, but cost has to be predictable."
- Data residency: EU and NA regional splits, some content restricted to on-prem VPC.

Indexing & scale:
- Corpus: ~12M source documents (avg 12k words), currently planning 60-80M chunks after sentence-aware chunking.
- Storage: expected ~4TB embeddings (float16), desire PQ/quantization to reduce footprint. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching.

Chunking strategy discussion notes:
- Team prefers sentence-boundary chunking with target 800-1500 token chunks, 20% overlap for context continuity.
- For spoken transcripts: aggressive boundary merging for utterance continuity; use speaker-break markers to avoid split names.
- Want a hybrid approach: long-form docs chunked for dense retrieval but keep title/metadata as separate high-priority vectors.
- Concern: chunk explosion with naive fixed windows; looking for metrics from Redwood on typical chunk:doc ratio and token distribution.

Retrieval + reranker plan notes:
- Retrieval: dense vector (bi-encoder) at scale as first pass -> recall focused.
- Reranker: cross-encoder for top-k (k=8-12) to improve precision for editorial workflows. Trade-off: cross-encoder adds inference latency and cost.
- Target SLOs: end-to-end p95 <= 450ms for small queries (editor UI), p99 <= 700ms acceptable for complex searches. Live API call SLA target for batch exports is lower priority.
- Cost goal: <$0.15 per interactive query end-to-end with reranking applied; they'd accept higher for admin workflows.
- Optimizations discussed: batching top-k rerank in GPU pools (Dedicated), caching reranker outputs for frequent queries, warm prefix caching for common content, use of quantized bi-encoder embeddings to cut memory.

Evaluation/POC plan (agreed):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Ingest 2M representative docs -> evaluate chunker variants (window, sentence, adaptive) and measure chunk count + token distribution.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Run retrieval baseline (faiss-style + Redwood runtime) -> measure recall@10/100, latency distribution.
- Phase 3 (3 weeks): Cross-encoder tuning on labeled editorial testset (3k queries) -> optimize MRR and precision@5 under latency constraints.
- Phase 4: Scale run to 10M chunks, quantify cost per query and RAM/GPU sizing.

Operational notes / asks to Redwood: 
- Need clear guidance on Dedicated pool sizing for reranker GPU allocation (expected concurrent editors ~120 during peak).
- Want automated suggestions from Redwood Optimize for batching and quantization profiles per workload.
- Request: security FAQ answers + SOC2 certificate for legal review (see linked drive doc).

Sales/contract notes: 
- Procurement: Head of Technology will push for Private deployment if Dedicated pricing can't meet cost predictability.
- Procurement timeline: decision target by 2026-04; procurement to start immediately post-successful POC.
